Confidence increases from 0.45 to 0.65, but remains moderate because confirmatory molecular and staging results are not yet available.

node-12.label: Staging imaging (e.g., CT/PET) has been recommended but results are not yet available

why.why: The pathologist states the violaceous annular patches are consistent with classic patch-stage mycosis fungoides, and the laboratory physician reports H&E epidermotropism. Together with negative Wood lamp and resistance to antifungals/topical steroids, this raises confidence from 0.45 to 0.70, while definitive IHC/TCR/flow and staging confirmation remain pending.

node-14.label: Primary cutaneous CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder (e.g., primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma)

why.why: Expert consensus and the reported epidermotropism favor patch-stage mycosis fungoides rather than a CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder, which more often forms nodules or ulcerated lesions. Confidence is reduced from 0.06 to 0.04.

The new expert-supported emphasis on epidermotropism and patch-stage mycosis fungoides makes cutaneous B-cell lymphoma less likely, as B-cell lymphomas usually form firm nodules or plaques without this pattern. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.03.

node-16.label: Other cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (e.g., Sézary syndrome, peripheral T-cell lymphoma)

why.why: Expert analyses continue to focus on patch-stage mycosis fungoides; the absence of erythroderma, generalized lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms argues against Sézary syndrome or aggressive peripheral T-cell lymphoma. Confidence is reduced from 0.04 to 0.02.
